title: ubuntu-cpc: discover partitions based on types
commit_message:
ubuntu-cpc: discover partitions based on types
functions: enable support for partition discovery via types
diff:
diff --git a/debian/changelog b/debian/changelog
index 63777ee..5fca180 100644
--- a/debian/changelog
+++ b/debian/changelog
@@ -1,3 +1,11 @@
+livecd-rootfs (26.04.3) resolute; urgency=medium
+
+  * functions: Use GPT partition table and type UUID to find the root/boot/EFI
+    partitions. Default to the pre-defined partition IDs (resp. 1, 14, 15) if
+    the type UUID lookup fails.
+
+ -- Gauthier Jolly <gauthier.jolly@canonical.com>  Tue, 28 Oct 2025 09:44:24 +0100
+
 livecd-rootfs (26.04.2) resolute; urgency=medium
 
   [ Gauthier Jolly ]
diff --git a/live-build/functions b/live-build/functions
index 6356166..84ad5f4 100644
--- a/live-build/functions
+++ b/live-build/functions
@@ -81,6 +81,10 @@ make_ext4_partition() {
 }
 
 mount_image() {
+    # Usage: mount_image DISK_IMAGE ROOT_PARTITION
+    # Mounts the disk image and sets up loop devices.
+    # If ROOT_PARTITION is negative, tries to auto-detect root partition.
+
     trap clean_loops EXIT
     backing_img="$1"
     local rootpart="$2"
@@ -92,14 +96,20 @@ mount_image() {
         exit 1
     fi
 
+    # Find the rootfs location
+    if [ "${rootpart}" -ge 0 ]; then
+        echo "Using specified root partition '${rootpart}' to locate rootfs." >&2
+        rootfs_dev_mapper="${loop_device}p${rootpart}"
+    else
+        echo "Auto-detecting root partition based on type UUID to locate rootfs." >&2
+        rootfs_dev_mapper="$(get_root_partition_device_path ${loop_device} ${ARCH})"
+    fi
+
     # As explained in excruciating detail in LP: #2045586, losetup
     # races with udev in a way that can cause partition device files
     # to briefly vanish. systemd docs say we can hold udev off by using
     # flocks: https://systemd.io/BLOCK_DEVICE_LOCKING/
     # `udevadm lock` isn't yet usable in Ubuntu, so we'll use flock for now
-
-    # Find the rootfs location
-    rootfs_dev_mapper="${loop_device}p${rootpart}"
     if flock -x ${loop_device} [ ! -b "${rootfs_dev_mapper}" ]; then
         echo "${rootfs_dev_mapper} is not a block device";
         exit 1
@@ -252,18 +262,97 @@ get_lowerdirs_for_pass () {
     echo "${lowerlayers#:}"
 }
 
+get_device_partition_by_type_uuid() {
+    # Usage: get_device_partition_by_type_uuid TYPE_UUID BLOCK_DEVICE
+    # Returns the first partition device path for the given TYPE_UUID on BLOCK_DEVICE
+    local type_uuid="$1"
+    local block_device="$2"
+
+    udevadm lock --device="${block_device}" \
+        lsblk -o PATH,PARTTYPE -nr "${block_device}" | \
+            awk -v type_uuid="${type_uuid}" \
+                '$2 == type_uuid { print $1; exit 0 }'
+}
+
+get_esp_device_path() {
+    # Usage: get_esp_device_path BLOCK_DEVICE
+    # Returns the partition device path for the UEFI ESP on BLOCK_DEVICE
+    # using TYPE_UUID lookup, with a fallback to p15.
+
+    local block_device="$1"
+    local esp_type_uuid="c12a7328-f81f-11d2-ba4b-00a0c93ec93b"
+
+    by_type=$(get_device_partition_by_type_uuid "${esp_type_uuid}" "${block_device}")
+    if [ -n "${by_type}" ]; then
+        echo "${by_type}"
+        return 0
+    fi
+
+    # Fallback to partition 15 for UEFI ESP
+    echo "Failed to find ESP with GPT type UUID on ${block_device}" >&2
+    echo "Falling back to partition 15 for UEFI ESP" >&2
+    echo "${block_device}p15"
+}
+
+get_boot_partition_device_path() {
+    # Usage: get_boot_partition_device_path BLOCK_DEVICE
+    # Returns the partition device path for the XBOOTLDR on BLOCK_DEVICE
+    # using TYPE_UUID lookup, with a fallback to p13.
+
+    local block_device="$1"
+    local xbootldr_type_uuid="bc13c2ff-59e6-4262-a352-b275fd6f7172"
+
+    by_type=$(get_device_partition_by_type_uuid "${xbootldr_type_uuid}" "${block_device}")
+    if [ -n "${by_type}" ]; then
+        echo "${by_type}"
+        return 0
+    fi
+
+    # Fallback to partition 13 for XBOOTLDR
+    echo "Failed to find boot partition with GPT type UUID on ${block_device}" >&2
+    echo "Falling back to partition 13 for XBOOTLDR" >&2
+    echo "${block_device}p13"
+}
+
+get_root_partition_device_path() {
+    # Usage: get_root_partition_device_path BLOCK_DEVICE ARCH
+    # Returns the partition device path for the rootfs on BLOCK_DEVICE
+    # using TYPE_UUID lookup, with a fallback to p1.
+
+    local block_device="$1"
+    local arch="$2"
+
+    local rootfs_type_uuid="$(gpt_root_partition_uuid ${arch})"
+
+    by_type=$(get_device_partition_by_type_uuid "${rootfs_type_uuid}" "${block_device}")
+    if [ -n "${by_type}" ]; then
+        echo "${by_type}"
+        return 0
+    fi
+
+    # Fallback to partition 1 for rootfs
+    echo "Failed to find root partition with GPT type UUID on ${block_device}" >&2
+    echo "Falling back to partition 1 for rootfs" >&2
+    echo "${block_device}p1"
+}
+
 mount_disk_image() {
+    # Usage: mount_disk_image DISK_IMAGE MOUNTPOINT ROOT_PARTITION
+    # Mounts rootfs, boot, and EFI partitions inside the disk image to MOUNTPOINT.
+    # If ROOT_PARTITION is not specified, defaults to 1.
+    # If ROOT_PARTITION is specified but negative, tries to auto-detect root partition.
+
     local disk_image=${1}
     local mountpoint=${2}
     local rootpart=${3:-1}
     mount_image ${disk_image} "${rootpart}"
     mount_partition "${rootfs_dev_mapper}" $mountpoint
 
-    local boot_dev="${loop_device}p13"
+    local boot_dev="$(get_boot_partition_device_path ${loop_device})"
     if flock -x ${loop_device} \
         [ -b ${boot_dev} -a -e $mountpoint/boot ]; then
         # Only mount if assumed boot_dev is XBOOTLDR type
-        if sgdisk -i13 "${loop_device}" | grep -i BC13C2FF-59E6-4262-A352-B275FD6F7172 ; then
+        if lsblk -o PARTUUID "${boot_dev}" | grep -i BC13C2FF-59E6-4262-A352-B275FD6F7172 ; then
             flock -x ${loop_device} mount "${boot_dev}" $mountpoint/boot
         fi
     fi
@@ -271,7 +360,7 @@ mount_disk_image() {
     # Having one partition mounted should avoid udev-triggered partition
     # rescans on that device, so we no longer need to flock.
 
-    local uefi_dev="${loop_device}p15"
+    local uefi_dev="$(get_esp_device_path ${loop_device})"
     if [ -b ${uefi_dev} -a -e $mountpoint/boot/efi ]; then
         mount "${uefi_dev}" $mountpoint/boot/efi
     fi
@@ -312,7 +401,7 @@ umount_partition() {
 umount_disk_image() {
     mountpoint="$1"
 
-    local uefi_dev="${loop_device}p15"
+    local uefi_dev="$(get_esp_device_path ${loop_device})"
     if [ -e "$mountpoint/boot/efi" -a -b "$uefi_dev" ]; then
 	# zero fill free space in UEFI partition
 	cat < /dev/zero > "$mountpoint/boot/efi/bloat_file" 2> /dev/null || true
@@ -1443,4 +1532,4 @@ gpt_root_partition_uuid() {
     esac
 
     echo "${ROOTFS_PARTITION_TYPE}"
-}
\ No newline at end of file
+}
diff --git a/live-build/ubuntu-cpc/hooks.d/base/disk-image-uefi.binary b/live-build/ubuntu-cpc/hooks.d/base/disk-image-uefi.binary
index ca7c796..5637bca 100755
--- a/live-build/ubuntu-cpc/hooks.d/base/disk-image-uefi.binary
+++ b/live-build/ubuntu-cpc/hooks.d/base/disk-image-uefi.binary
@@ -76,8 +76,8 @@ create_partitions() {
 }
 
 create_and_mount_boot_partitions() {
-    uefi_dev="${loop_device}p15"
-    boot_dev="${loop_device}p13"
+    uefi_dev="$(get_esp_device_path ${loop_device})"
+    boot_dev="$(get_boot_partition_device_path ${loop_device})"
     mountpoint="$1"
 
     mkfs.vfat -F 32 -n UEFI "${uefi_dev}"
@@ -201,7 +201,7 @@ disk_image=binary/boot/disk-uefi.ext4
 
 create_empty_disk_image "${disk_image}"
 create_partitions "${disk_image}"
-mount_image "${disk_image}" 1
+mount_image "${disk_image}" -1
 
 # Copy the chroot in to the disk
 make_ext4_partition "${rootfs_dev_mapper}"
